court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Additional District Judge, (Fast Track Court), Ariyalur; District Munsif, Ariyalur

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Veerappan, Rajakumari, Gandhimathi, Nithiya, Minor Paraveen (rep by mother and guardian Rajalakshmi)

facts_of_case: Suit property partitioned among family members. Plaintiff's father divorced second defendant due to bad reputation. Plaintiff claims relief against judgment and decree dated 24.04.2008.

legal_principles.principle: The factum of marriage cannot be proved merely by placing reliance on birth extract and other documents.
legal_principles.held: The courts below have presumed the existence of marriage only by placing reliance on birth extract and other documents, which cannot be the basis for the proof of marriage.
cited_cases: V. Leela and others vs D. Rajammal (Died), Gopal reported in 1993 II MLJ 17

legal_principles.principle: A judgment in an earlier suit can operate as constructive res judicata against a present plaintiff.
legal_principles.held: It is also further argued that the first defendant had not raised the issue about the divorce of the second defendant by Singaram or self respect marriage in the earlier suit and the first defendant is the dishonest woman, black mailer and instigated the plaintiff and file the present suit.

outcome.final_order: Second Appeal filed under Section 100 of C.P.C. is allowed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a second appeal under Section 100 C.P.C.
preparing a judgment and decree in a property dispute case
arguing a point of law in a Hindu Marriage Act case
